name: Pulse
line: You run the floor for one shift: people, damage, incomplete orders, delays, and a clean handover at the end.

routine.do: Read the last handover before the briefing, not after the first problem.
Log each damaged unit where it happens, with its stage and cause.
Log every order that leaves without all its items or parcels.
In a hotel, log every exception the night audit finds, with its stage and cause, before the audit closes.
Before you write the handover, look at the whole shift in one picture.
Hand over open issues with an owner and a time, not a story.
See whether late routes started at the dock or on the road.
Ask why until you reach something you can change.
Read the actions overdue first, then this week's, then what was verified. Ten minutes, the list is the agenda.
Open the board at the huddle, read the five letters and the agenda, and give every red day an action with an owner and a date.
Walk the same areas on the same day, score what you see, and give every finding at 2 or below an owner before you leave the floor.
Log what happened yesterday, read the talk of the day at the briefing and ask who saw a near miss.
Log every item handed in with its tag number, contact the guest the same day and clear the items due for a decision before the shift ends.
Keep every room's status current as the work happens, clean the queue from the top, and copy the summary into the shift handover.
Log every complaint while the guest is still with you, walk through LEARN, resolve it within the target and call the guest back before the shift ends.

name: Zenith
line: You lead the shift leads. You read an area's numbers week by week and decide where the next hour of attention goes.

routine.do: Read yesterday in one view: on time, undamaged, complete and complaints.
Find out whether it is clarity, skill, capacity, process or ownership before you push.
Sort the week's losses and start with the few causes behind most of them.
Read the logs of your shifts week by week: rates, the trend and what is still open.
Check with your shift leads where route delays begin.
Tell a real change from a normal bad day before you react.
Write the problem on one A3 before you fix it: the number, the root cause, one owner per countermeasure, and the date you will check.
Answer every new idea within the week, move each card one honest step, and name the idea of the month in front of the team.
Walk the matrix with each team lead, update the levels you saw on the floor, take a snapshot and give every single point of failure a trainee and a date.
Log the shift of each machine with its stops by reason, then attack the biggest of the six losses with an owner and a date.
Paste last night's figures from the night audit, read the morning report at the meeting and act on the KPI the tool puts first.
Walk your layer's questions where the work is done, answer each with yes or no against the standard, and give every no you cannot fix on the spot an owner before you leave the floor.
Send last week's report to your manager and put its three priorities into the Action Tracker.
Inspect every checkout and VIP room before release, and coach on the fault that fails most.
Print the work list on Monday and give every overdue task on a critical asset a date this week.
Read the signals before the morning meeting, take the first high ones to the floor and give each one an owner, a 5 Whys or a date.
Read today's departures and stay-overs after the night audit, check the attendants needed against the schedule, and hand every attendant the printed sheet of their section.
Open today's standard, tick each task as you do it, and give every miss a reason before the handover.
Paste next week's volume forecast before the roster closes and close every shift that is short of hours with a move, overtime or agency booking.
Walk one area with the people who work there, close or re-date its overdue measures and check the effect of the ones done.

name: Lumen
line: You look at the whole system: find where a problem really sits, prove it with data, and change the process so it stays fixed.

routine.do: Reach a root cause you can change before anyone proposes a fix.
Put the process on a control chart and react only to real signals.
Rank the losses and choose the next improvement project.
Run it through Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve and Control.
Gather the people who do the work for fifteen minutes, fill the bones, vote, and leave with the likely causes as actions to verify on the floor.
Walk the changed steps with the team, rate each failure mode and give every high-priority row an action with an owner and a date.
Measure twenty values before you change the process and twenty after, then let the test say whether the change is real.
Time one station for five cycles, compare it with takt and move the first element that fits.
Walk one value stream from the customer back, count every pile, and turn the largest wait into a kaizen burst with an owner.
Write the job as a standard with a reason for every key point, start a new version when it changes, and train the team on it.
Follow one job with the floor plan, draw its walks, and move the stop visited most next to where the work happens.
Review each project with its lead, tick what the next tollgate still needs, and ask the sponsor to sign the phases that are ready.
Import last month's demand, reorder every A SKU below its reorder point and move the top AX SKUs into the golden zone.
Time one changeover of the line with the longest stops, move everything external out of the stop and print the new changeover standard for the machine.
Open an 8D the day the customer complains: contain it within 24 hours, then verify the root cause and the escape point before you choose the fix.

name: Atlas
line: Carry your experience into the next role: a designed CV, an ATS CV and a matching cover letter.

routine.do: Add one result with a number to your CV while you still remember it.
Check your CV against the job ad, the way screening software reads it.
Write the letter for this company, not for any company.
